title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 75 (Compensation after rightful rescission)

content.overview: Section 75 provides that a person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for damage sustained through the contract's non-fulfilment. The statutory trigger is rightful rescission; a party cannot assume that any termination or refusal to perform satisfies that condition. The Act's illustration concerns a theatre manager who rescinds after a singer wilfully fails to perform as agreed. Current-amendment status and case-law treatment remain subject to further verification.

sections.heading: Statutory rule and trigger
sections.body: Section 75 states that a person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment of the contract. Analyse the rightfulness of rescission before moving to the compensation question.

sections.heading: Rightful rescission
sections.body: Identify the contractual obligation, the other party's non-fulfilment, the facts said to justify rescission and the legal basis for treating the rescission as rightful. Do not equate every cancellation, termination notice or walk-away with rightful rescission without analysing the governing contract and law.

sections.heading: Damage caused by non-fulfilment
sections.body: Identify each head of damage said to have been sustained through non-fulfilment and establish its causal connection to the contract's failure. Section 75's short text does not itself quantify damages; the applicable rules and facts must support the amount claimed.

sections.heading: Relationship with Sections 73 and 74
sections.body: Section 73 states the general rule for compensation for loss caused by breach; Section 74 deals with a named sum or penalty stipulation. Section 75 specifically addresses compensation for damage sustained by a person who rightfully rescinds. Identify the actual statutory trigger and avoid treating these provisions as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Statutory illustration
sections.body: The Act illustrates a singer who agrees to perform twice weekly for two months, wilfully absents herself on the sixth night, and is met with the theatre manager's rescission. The manager may claim compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment. Apply the illustration only to its material facts.

sections.heading: Evidence and application
sections.body: Preserve the contract, performance schedule, notices and correspondence, evidence of non-fulfilment, facts supporting the right to rescind, and records supporting each claimed loss. State the rescission issue separately from the amount of compensation.

examples.title: Rightful rescission after repeated non-performance
examples.body: A service provider's material non-fulfilment gives the other party a legally sufficient basis to rescind. If the rescission is rightful, Section 75 may support compensation for damage sustained through the non-fulfilment, subject to proof and applicable law.

examples.title: Singer and theatre manager
examples.body: The Act's illustration describes a singer contracted to perform two nights each week for two months who wilfully absents herself on the sixth night. The theatre manager rescinds and may claim compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment.

hypotheticals.question: A party sends a termination email after the other side misses a deadline. Is Section 75 automatically satisfied?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. First establish whether the rescission was rightful under the contract and governing law. Then identify damage sustained through non-fulfilment and support the causal connection and amount.

hypotheticals.question: A party rightfully rescinds but cannot identify any damage sustained. What does Section 75 itself establish?
hypotheticals.analysis: The section recognises entitlement to compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment. It does not itself establish a fixed amount; the claimed damage and applicable measure require separate analysis.

hypotheticals.question: How should a Section 75 claim be distinguished from a stipulated penalty claim?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify whether the case turns on rightful rescission and damage through non-fulfilment under Section 75, or on a sum named or penalty stipulated for breach under Section 74. The factual and contractual triggers differ.

illustrations: Section 75 illustration: a singer contracts to perform two nights each week for two months, wilfully absents herself on the sixth night, and the theatre manager rescinds; the manager is entitled to claim compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment.

enhancement.definition: Section 75 entitles a person who rightfully rescinds a contract to compensation for damage sustained through the contract's non-fulfilment.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Rightful rescission is a prerequisite to the Section 75 entitlement; the damage claimed must be damage sustained through non-fulfilment, and its amount must be supported by the applicable law and facts.

essentialIngredients: Identify the contract and the obligation that was not fulfilled
Establish facts and legal basis showing rescission was rightful

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 75 is headed 'Party rightfully rescinding contract, entitled to compensation'. Its operative rule states that a person who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for damage sustained through non-fulfilment. The analysis therefore has two distinct stages: determine whether the rescission was rightful, then assess the damage sustained through non-fulfilment. The statutory illustration concerns a singer who wilfully fails to perform as agreed and a theatre manager who rescinds. Section 75 does not set a fixed amount of compensation. Its relationship with Sections 73 and 74 should be explained by reference to each provision's own trigger.
examples: A party rightfully rescinds after legally sufficient non-fulfilment and claims evidenced damage caused by that failure.
The statutory singer/theatre illustration is used to explain the right-to-rescind and damage elements, not to create an automatic formula.
distinctions: Section 73 sets the general rule for compensation for loss caused by breach and excludes remote and indirect loss.
Section 74 addresses a named sum payable on breach or another stipulation by way of penalty, with reasonable compensation capped by the named sum or penalty.
Section 75 specifically requires rightful rescission and damage sustained through non-fulfilment.
problemApplication: State why rescission was legally rightful on the facts.
List each claimed head of damage and prove its causal connection.
Quantify damage under the applicable law and evidence.
Distinguish any separate Section 73 or Section 74 issue.
Conclude on entitlement without assuming a fixed award.
keyTakeaways: The claimed damage must have been sustained through non-fulfilment.
The statutory illustration is fact-specific; Section 75 does not set a fixed amount.
Distinguish Section 75's trigger from the general breach rule in Section 73 and penalty stipulations in Section 74.
